{{nihongo|'''Gaisi Takeuti'''|竹内 外史|Takeuchi, Gaishi|extra=January 25, 1926 – May 10, 2017<ref>{{Cite web|author=Sam Buss|date=2017-05-10|url=https://list.math.cas.cz/pipermail/proof-complexity/2017-May/000206.html|title=[Proof Complexity] Gaisi Takeuti|publisher=Proof-Complexity mailing list|access-date=2019-01-13}}</ref>}} was a Japanese [[mathematician]], known for his work in [[proof theory]].<ref>{{harvnb|Takeuti|2013}}.</ref>

After graduating from [[Tokyo University]], he went to [[Princeton University|Princeton]] to study under [[Kurt Gödel]]. 
<!-- Cite? He was one of the few people that Godel could feel comfortable with. --> 
He later became a professor at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]]. Takeuti was president (2003–2009) of the [[Kurt Gödel Society]], having worked on the book ''Memoirs of a Proof Theorist: Godel and Other Logicians''.  His goal was to prove the [[consistency]] of the real numbers.  To this end, [[Takeuti's conjecture]] speculates that a [[sequent calculus|sequent]] formalisation of [[second-order logic]] has [[cut-elimination theorem|cut-elimination]].<ref>{{harvnb|Takeuti|1953}}. An erratum to this article was published in the same journal as {{harv|Takeuti|1954}}.</ref>  He is also known for his work on [[ordinal notation|ordinal diagrams]] with Akiko Kino.
